description: The UCS Satellite Database is a listing of the operational satellites orbiting Earth, compiled by experts at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS) from open-source information as a research tool for specialists and non-specialists. The latest release counts more than 7,560 operational satellites. It contains 28 types of data for each satellite: technical information such as mass, power, launch date and expected lifetime; orbital parameters (orbit class, apogee, perigee, inclination and period); purpose; and the countries and organisations that own, operate and built it. It is downloaded free of charge as an Excel file or a tab-delimited text file, with a variant containing only official names. The page states the database was last updated on 1 May 2023, so it misses the rapid growth of large constellations since then; open-source compilation also means military satellites and some parameters are incomplete. No licence is stated. It is used to describe the space segment that GNSS, telecom and Earth observation services depend on, to count assets exposed to space weather and debris, and as reference data for interdependency models of satellite services; related records are ESA DISCOS and the NOAA SWPC products in this catalogue.
